tasks.task: Establish site setup and exclusion zones
tasks.scope: Demarcate laydown area, crane operating zone, exclusion zones around unbraced and partially braced panels. Set up site signage and access control.
hazards: Trip hazard from ground-level obstructions, cables, or packing materials in laydown and exclusion zones
Struck-by hazard from mobile equipment moving through site during demarcation setup
Inadequate exclusion zone boundaries allowing unauthorised entry into crane operating zone
tasks.dominant_hazard: Struck-by from mobile equipment in active laydown area
controls: Barricade crane operating zone with Class A or B barriers on all four sides, minimum 2 m from crane base.
Erect exclusion zone signage around unbraced and partially braced panels: warning signs every 3 m, minimum 1.5 m high.
Demarcate laydown area with high-visibility tape or paint, clearly separate from pedestrian and vehicle routes.
Segregate mobile equipment movement routes from pedestrian access using physical barriers or permanent separation.
Check ground-level area for cables, packing, and debris before allowing workers to enter laydown zone.
Establish single entry/exit point with sign-in/sign-out log and access control at each shift start.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow worker access to laydown area until: all exclusion zone signage and barriers are installed and site induction completed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: crane operating zone or exclusion zone barriers are missing, damaged, or removed during shift.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unauthorised personnel enter crane operating zone or exclusion zone.
🛑 STOP WORK if: trip hazards (cables, packing, debris) accumulate in laydown or pedestrian areas without removal.
admin: Complete site induction including exclusion zone rules, struck-by hazards, and emergency assembly point before each worker enters site.
Conduct daily toolbox talk on crane movement schedule and active exclusion zones.
Record all exclusion zone breaches and corrective actions in site safety log.
Confirm first aider present on site before demarcation starts; display first aid location signage.
ppe: High-visibility vest (Class 2 or 3) for all workers in laydown and demarcation area.
Safety helmet for all workers on site.
steel-capped footwear, slip-resistant) for all workers in laydown area.
High-visibility clothing for traffic control personnel complying with AS 1742.3.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.evidence: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Confirm crane lift plan and positioning
tasks.scope: Verify crane lift plan with structural engineer. Position mobile crane on firm, level ground. Establish crane exclusion radius and communication protocol.
hazards: Crane overturn or loss of stability if ground is inadequately compacted or uneven beneath crane outriggers
Crane failure or boom collapse if load plan does not match actual panel weights or rigging configuration
Collision between crane and site boundary, temporary works, or adjacent structures during slew or repositioning
Communication breakdown between crane operator and ground crew, leading to uncontrolled or unsafe lift
tasks.dominant_hazard: Crane overturn or instability due to inadequate ground bearing
controls: Obtain written lift plan from structural engineer confirming load weight, rigging configuration, and crane capacity before positioning crane.
Check ground bearing capacity with geotechnical report or site engineer; mark soft spots, water pooling, or unstable areas with tape.
Position mobile crane on firm, level ground with outriggers fully extended and bearing plates under each pad.
Establish crane exclusion radius of at least 1.5 times boom length; barricade with tape and signage.
Brief all site workers and contractors on exclusion zone before crane operation starts.
Establish two-way radio communication between crane operator and appointed ground spotter; confirm radio channel and test before lift.
Position ground spotter with clear line of sight to crane operator and load; keep spotter outside exclusion zone.
Stop all other work within exclusion zone during crane positioning and lift operations.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not position crane until: written lift plan is signed by structural engineer and ground bearing capacity is confirmed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ground beneath outrigger pads is soft, uneven, or subsiding during load application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: radio communication is lost or unclear between operator and ground spotter.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker or vehicle enters the crane exclusion zone during lift or slew operations.
admin: Retain signed lift plan on site before crane arrival.
Provide ground bearing assessment to crane operator.
Brief spotter and workers on exclusion zone in toolbox meeting.
Record spotter radio check in site diary.
Submit SafeWork NSW notification before crane operation.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.evidence: Written confirmation from site engineer and visual inspection of ground contact

responsibility.SUP: Supervise crane positioning, verify lift plan signed, confirm ground bearing, authorise lift start
responsibility.WKR: Position crane per plan, maintain exclusion zone, communicate via radio, report ground subsidence

tasks.task: Lift and position CLT wall panels
tasks.scope: Using mobile crane, lift 36 CLT panels from laydown area and position on slab per structural engineer erection sequence. Lower panel to final position under crane supervision.
hazards: Uncontrolled swing or drift of panel during lift if rigging fails, spreader bars slip, or wind gusts occur
Panel dropped or released during lift if crane hook fails, sling breaks, or rigging hardware is undersized
Struck-by hazard to personnel below panel if load falls or swings into exclusion zone
Crane boom collision with adjacent panels, temporary works, or site boundary during positioning
Ground personnel crushed or struck if panel is lowered onto them during final positioning
tasks.dominant_hazard: Panel dropped or uncontrolled swing during lift, striking personnel or structures
controls: Verify crane operator holds current Class L crane licence for mobile crane before starting work.
Confirm lifting plan signed by structural engineer and crane supervisor before first panel lift.
Confirm all slings, shackles, spreader bars and rigging hardware certified and load-rated for 150% of panel weight.
Establish exclusion zone minimum 1.5 × panel height around lift path; barricade with tape and stop all personnel entry.
Position dedicated banksman at ground level in full view of crane operator; use two-way radio throughout lift.
Brief all personnel within 50 m of lift before first panel lift on exclusion zone, hand signals, and stop-work triggers.
Check wind speed before each lift; stop work if sustained wind exceeds 20 km/h or gusts exceed 30 km/h.
Lower panel slowly under constant crane supervision; position spotters on slab to guide final placement without personnel under load.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not lift first panel until: lifting plan signed by engineer, exclusion zone barricaded, banksman and spotters briefed and in position.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not lower panel to final position until: slab location verified against plan, personnel cleared from drop zone, spotters confirm safe ground placement area.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed sustained above 20 km/h or gust speed above 30 km/h.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any personnel observed inside exclusion zone during lift.
🛑 STOP WORK if: banksman loses line-of-sight to crane operator or rigging shows visible wear, damage, or deformation.
admin: make sure SafeWork NSW notification submitted before crane mobilisation.
Verify structural engineer's erection sequence document on site and followed step-by-step.
Maintain daily site diary recording each panel lift, weather conditions, and any incidents.
ppe: High-visibility vest (Class D or E) for all personnel on slab and within 50 m of lift zone.
Hard hat for all personnel within 100 m of lift zone.
Steel-capped boots for ground personnel positioning or spotting panels.
Hearing protection (earmuffs or plugs) during continuous crane operation.

monitoring.critical_control: Verify exclusion zone barricaded and no personnel inside before crane lifts panel.
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of barricade integrity and zone clear; banksman hand signal to operator; site diary entry

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Lift and position CLT wall
responsibility.WKR: Perform Lift and position CLT wall per SWMS

tasks.scope: Install bolts, brackets, and screws at all panel junction points per structural engineer drawing. Torque fasteners to specification. Verify alignment before final tightening.
hazards: Panel movement or drift during fastener installation if temporary props are under-loaded or become loose
Slip and fall from working on elevated slab edge or between panels at height
Crush hazard to fingers or hand from fastener installation tool slipping or bolt over-tightening
Fastener failure if torque specification is not met or fastener is inserted incorrectly, compromising structural integrity
tasks.dominant_hazard: Panel movement during fastening, compromising connection integrity or causing fall from height
controls: Verify structural engineer drawing and torque specification before starting fastener installation.
Check all temporary props are in place, tight, and supporting panels without movement.
Confirm panel alignment using spirit level or alignment jig before installing first fastener.
Install fasteners in sequence specified on engineer drawing—do not skip or reorder.
Torque each bolt to specification using calibrated torque wrench—recheck torque after 24 hours.
Wear eye protection
Use anti-slip footwear and maintain three-point contact when working at panel edge.
Stop work immediately if panel shifts, props loosen, or fastener sits misaligned.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not tighten fasteners until: all temporary props verified tight and panel confirmed level and aligned
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release from edge until: all fasteners torqued to specification and rechecked
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any temporary prop becomes loose or panel drifts during fastening
🛑 STOP WORK if: fastener cannot be inserted straight or torque wrench does not reach specification
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses three-point contact or feels unstable at height
admin: Provide calibrated torque wrench—calibration certificate current and on site.
Brief all workers on engineer drawing, torque specification, and fastener sequence before work starts.
Record torque values and fastener locations in site logbook or as-fitted schedule.
Supervisor to witness first fastener installation and recheck torque after 24 hours.

monitoring.critical_control: Check panel is level and all props tight before each fastener installation.
monitoring.frequency: before each fastener, recheck torque 24 hours after installation
monitoring.evidence: Site logbook entry with torque values, as-fitted schedule, witness signature on first fastener, recalibration certificate on torque wrench

responsibility.WKR: Perform Install permanent structural connections per SWMS

tasks.task: Prepare prop base locations and packing
tasks.scope: check slab bearing for all 23 prop bases. Install timber packing on uneven slab at props 6 and 10 per Stora Enso bracing plan. Confirm level and bearing capacity.
hazards: Localised slab failure or bearing plate punching if packing is insufficient or unevenly loaded
Trip hazard from timber packing and prop bases protruding across walkways
Structural instability if prop bases are not level, causing uneven load distribution and panel racking
tasks.dominant_hazard: Slab bearing failure from inadequate packing or uneven load distribution
controls: Check slab bearing surface at all 23 prop base locations for cracks, spalling, or uneven wear before installing props.
Install timber packing at props 6 and 10 per Stora Enso bracing plan dimensions and species specified.
Confirm packing is level using spirit level across the bearing plate and slab surface — maximum 5 mm total variance.
Verify bearing capacity of slab at each prop location against design load — obtain structural engineer confirmation in writing.
Barricade prop bases and packing with high-visibility tape and warning signs to prevent trip hazards across walkways.
Record slab condition, packing installation details, and bearing confirmation in site diary before props are loaded.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install props until: structural engineer confirms slab bearing capacity is adequate for design load
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not load props until: all packing is level and barricaded, and slab condition record is complete
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: slab shows active cracking, spalling, or failure during packing installation or level check
🛑 STOP WORK if: packing settles or shifts after installation, causing prop bases to become uneven
🛑 STOP WORK if: structural engineer advises slab bearing capacity is insufficient for design load
admin: Obtain Stora Enso bracing plan and confirm packing specifications (timber species, dimensions, grade) before site delivery.
make sure structural engineer has inspected slab condition report and confirmed bearing capacity in writing.
Brief all workers on prop base locations, barricade zones, and trip hazard controls before work starts.
Record slab bearing inspection, packing installation, level confirmation, and engineer approval in site diary.
Retain written bearing capacity confirmation and packing installation record on file for duration of props on site.

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.evidence: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Prepare prop base locations and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Prepare prop base locations and per SWMS

tasks.task: Plumb and stabilise panel with temporary props
tasks.scope: Install and adjust push-pull props (10x F5, 13x F3) at each panel. Plumb panel to vertical tolerance. Confirm all props loaded and secure before releasing crane hook.
hazards: Panel collapse or tilt if props are not fully loaded or become dislodged during plumbing adjustment
Struck-by hazard from prop failure or sudden panel movement if props are incorrectly adjusted or unsecured
Crush hazard to hands or feet if prop adjustment hardware slips or prop base shifts during loading
Incomplete prop installation allowing panel to remain unstable, creating hazard for subsequent work
tasks.dominant_hazard: Panel collapse or uncontrolled tilt if props are not fully loaded or secured
controls: Confirm engineer-approved prop schedule and panel load distribution before starting prop installation.
Check each prop (F5 and F3) for damage, bent sections, or deformation before use.
Install props in sequence specified on drawings, starting from lowest load-bearing positions.
Load each prop progressively using threaded adjustment, monitoring plumb level continuously.
Plumb panel to vertical tolerance using spirit level or laser plumb on at least two faces.
Confirm all prop adjustment hardware is tight and base plates fully seated on stable ground.
Test each loaded prop by hand pressure to verify no movement or slippage before release.
Obtain written sign-off from supervisor confirming all props loaded and panel stable.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release crane hook until: supervisor has physically checked all prop base plates are fully seated and all adjustment hardware is torqued tight.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to next panel until: current panel is plumbed to tolerance and all props tested stable with hand pressure.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any prop shows visible deformation, cracking, or permanent bending during adjustment.
🛑 STOP WORK if: panel cannot be plumbed to tolerance or props cannot be fully loaded without tilting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any prop base slips, shifts, or sinks into ground during loading or plumbing.
admin: Verify engineer-approved prop schedule and load distribution plan is on site and accessible.
Brief all workers on prop installation sequence and plumbing tolerance before work starts.
Record plumb readings and supervisor sign-off for each panel in site logbook.
Establish exclusion zone around panel and props — no access except installation team.

monitoring.critical_control: Supervisor hand-tests each loaded prop for movement before crane release.
monitoring.frequency: before each prop installation complete and before crane hook release
monitoring.evidence: Written sign-off in site logbook confirming all props secure; plumb readings recorded.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Plumb and stabilise panel with
responsibility.WKR: Perform Plumb and stabilise panel with per SWMS

tasks.task: Release crane hook and repeat panel installation
tasks.scope: Release crane hook only after props confirmed loaded and panel stable. Return to sequence 4 and repeat for remaining 35 panels. Maintain exclusion zones around unbraced panels.
hazards: Panel falls or becomes unstable if props are not confirmed loaded or if hook is released prematurely
Personnel struck-by falling panel if crane hook is released before props are verified secure
Cumulative instability from multiple partially propped panels if release sequence does not verify each panel independently
Unauthorised entry into exclusion zone around unbraced panels by personnel or mobile equipment
tasks.dominant_hazard: Panel collapse if hook released before props confirmed loaded and secure
controls: Confirm props loaded by placing full weight on panel — check for movement or settlement before signalling hook release.
Release crane hook only after spotter verbally confirms props secure and panel stable.
Establish exclusion zone minimum 1.5× panel height around unbraced panels — barricade and post warning signs.
Brief all site personnel on exclusion zone before each panel lift — confirm understanding.
Stop work if panel shows any movement, settlement, or instability before props are confirmed fully loaded.
Return to sequence 4 and repeat panel installation method for each remaining panel — do not vary sequence or method.
Prohibit unauthorised entry into exclusion zone — position personnel to monitor zone perimeter during each lift and release.
Complete release check sheet for each panel — record prop confirmation, hook release time, and spotter name.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release crane hook until: spotter confirms visual and physical check that props are loaded and panel is stable and level.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: panel shows any movement, tilting, or settlement during prop loading.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unauthorised personnel or mobile equipment enter exclusion zone around unbraced panels.
🛑 STOP WORK if: props are not confirmed loaded before hook release is signalled.
admin: Appoint competent spotter — trained in panel stability and prop-loading verification — for each lift and release cycle.
Prepare panel release check sheet — record panel number, prop confirmation, release time, spotter name, date.
Conduct toolbox briefing before starting sequence 6 — confirm exclusion zone boundary, release procedure, and stop-work triggers.
tell crane operator of hold point — no hook release until spotter gives verbal all-clear.
Maintain exclusion zone signage and barricade for entire duration of panel installation sequence — refresh daily.

monitoring.critical_control: Spotter confirms prop loaded and panel stable before hook release signal given.
monitoring.frequency: Before each panel hook release — continuous visual and physical verification
monitoring.evidence: Signed panel release check sheet per panel; photographic record of prop loading confirmation; exclusion zone barricade and signage in place

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Release crane hook and repeat
responsibility.WKR: Perform Release crane hook and repeat per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove temporary props on engineer release
tasks.scope: Remove push-pull props only in sequence and method specified in engineer release letter. Verify panel stability and alignment after each prop removal. Document removal sequence.
hazards: Panel collapse or instability if props are removed out of sequence or in wrong order specified by engineer
Struck-by hazard from suddenly released prop or panel movement if removal procedure is not followed
Personnel crushed or trapped beneath prop or panel if stability verification is not completed after each removal
Cumulative drift or misalignment if panel stability is not confirmed independently after each prop removal
tasks.dominant_hazard: Panel collapse or sudden movement during prop removal sequence
controls: Obtain and read engineer release letter specifying prop removal sequence before starting work.
Brief all personnel on the exact removal order and hold points from engineer release letter.
Remove props only in the sequence and method specified in engineer release letter.
Stop and check panel for movement, drift, or misalignment immediately after each prop removal.
Record removal sequence, time, and stability confirmation for each prop in site log.
Use two spotters to monitor panel for visible movement or sound of cracking during removal.
Do not remove adjacent props in sequence without independent stability check between removals.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove next prop until: panel stability confirmed and recorded after previous prop removal
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start removal work until: engineer release letter received and removal sequence briefed to all personnel on site
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: panel shows visible movement, drift, or audible cracking after prop removal
🛑 STOP WORK if: removal sequence deviates from engineer release letter specification
🛑 STOP WORK if: stability check or documentation is skipped or incomplete for any prop removal
admin: Obtain engineer release letter and site-specific removal sequence instruction before work starts.
Hold pre-work meeting with all personnel to confirm removal sequence and hold points.
Assign dedicated spotter to monitor panel stability during each prop removal.
Record removal sequence, time, stability outcome, and any drift or movement in site log.
Keep engineer release letter and removal documentation on site for audit and inspection.

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.evidence: Site log entry with timestamp, prop ID, stability confirmation, and spotter sign-off; photographic evidence of panel alignment; engineer release letter on site.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove temporary props on engineer
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove temporary props on engineer per SWMS

tasks.task: Engineer inspection and temporary works hold
tasks.scope: Request structural engineer inspection of all panels, props, and connections. Obtain written engineer approval before any prop removal. Document hold point sign-off.
hazards: Incomplete or inadequate engineer inspection if inspector does not verify all prop loading, panel plumb, and connection torque
Unauthorised work commencement (prop removal) before engineer sign-off, leading to panel instability
Documentation loss or ambiguity of hold point, allowing premature or unsafe work progression
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inadequate engineer verification leading to work commencement on unstable panel configuration
controls: Obtain written structural engineer inspection report covering all panels, props, connections, and load paths before any prop removal.
Verify engineer has checked prop plumb, connection torque, panel alignment, and load distribution against design drawings.
Post engineer approval letter on site at the hold point location — accessible to all workers.
Prohibit any prop removal or panel adjustment until engineer sign-off document is sighted by site supervisor.
Record engineer name, inspection date, approval date, and signature on hold point log before work proceeds.
Brief all workers on hold point location and content — confirm understanding before commencement of any prop removal phase.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove any props or adjust panels until: Structural engineer written approval is obtained, dated, signed, and posted on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Any prop removal begins without sighted engineer approval letter.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Engineer report does not cover plumb, torque, or load verification of all panels in scope.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Hold point sign-off log is incomplete or unsigned by supervising engineer or site supervisor.
admin: Request structural engineer inspection before work package release.
Site supervisor to verify engineer credentials and check permit on file.
Maintain hold point sign-off log on site — record engineer name, date, and worker names briefed.
Keep engineer approval letter pinned at hold point for 7 days post-work or until panel removal complete.

monitoring.critical_control: Confirm structural engineer approval letter dated, signed, and on-site before any prop removal starts.
monitoring.evidence: Signed engineer report + hold point log entry with supervisor and engineer signature + photo of posted approval at hold point.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Engineer inspection and temporary works
responsibility.WKR: Perform Engineer inspection and temporary works per SWMS

tasks.scope: Visually check all 36 panels for damage, misalignment, or defects. Record defects and repair requirements. tell contractor before demobilisation.
hazards: Fall from height if inspector accesses panel upper surfaces or edges without fall protection
Struck-by hazard from unstable panel if defects indicate panel misalignment or inadequate bracing
Documentation failure if defects are not accurately recorded, leading to unidentified structural or safety issues
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during panel inspection at upper level
controls: Wear harness and lanyard attached to fixed anchor point before accessing panel upper surfaces or edges.
Check all anchor points and attachment hardware for damage, corrosion, or movement before use.
Complete fall arrest system inspection and tag before each shift starts.
Brief all inspectors on panel defect types, documentation format, and stop-work triggers before inspection starts.
Establish exclusion zone below inspection area — minimum 3 m radius — barricade and signage.
Document each defect with panel ID, defect type, location, and photograph in site logbook.
Assess panel alignment and bracing condition — stop work if panel shows lateral movement or tilting.
tell site supervisor immediately if defects indicate structural instability or safety risk.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not access panel upper surfaces until: harness, lanyard, and anchor point are checked, tagged, and confirmed load-bearing by supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not demobilise until: defect report is completed, photographed, and signed off by contractor representative.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: panel shows visible lateral movement, tilting, or separation from bracing during inspection.
🛑 STOP WORK if: harness or lanyard is damaged, torn, or shows signs of impact or wear.
🛑 STOP WORK if: anchor point shows corrosion, cracks, or movement when load tested by hand.
admin: Confirm fall arrest system is certified, tagged, and valid before issue to inspector.
Verify inspector holds current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and site induction.
Obtain written sign-off from contractor on defect severity and repair priority before demobilisation.
Record all defects, photographs, and corrective actions in site logbook for audit trail.
ppe: Full body harness — certified, adjusted, and tagged.
Lanyard — 1.8 m or less, shock absorber, attached to harness dorsal d-ring.

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each access and continuous during inspection
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of attachment, tag on harness valid and current, supervisor sign-off in logbook.

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion
responsibility.WKR: check per specification, photograph defects, report issues

tasks.task: Demobilise crane and remove support equipment
tasks.scope: Derig crane from site. Remove props, temporary bracing, and support equipment. Leave site clean and panels ready for next trade.
hazards: Struck-by hazard from crane or derrig equipment during demobilisation if exclusion zone is not maintained
Uncontrolled movement of props or temporary bracing during removal if not sequenced or secured
Trip hazard from scattered props, bracing, or packing materials during site clean-up
tasks.dominant_hazard: Struck-by from moving crane or derrig equipment during demobilisation
controls: Establish and maintain exclusion zone 1.5 times crane radius around derrig operations — no workers or vehicles enter until crane movement stops
Brief all site workers on derrig sequence and exclusion zone boundaries before crane movement starts
Remove props and temporary bracing in reverse order of installation — follow engineer-approved removal sequence
Secure all loose props, bracing, and packing materials before moving or stacking — use straps or netting to prevent scatter
Lower all equipment and materials to ground level under control — do not drop or throw from height
Segregate demobilised equipment into designated lay-down areas — prevent trip hazards across work zones
Sweep and clear all scattered debris, packing, and materials from site before handing over to next trade
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start crane derrig until: exclusion zone is established, barricaded, and all workers briefed on boundaries and stop signals
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker or vehicle enters exclusion zone during crane movement
🛑 STOP WORK if: props or bracing are not secured and risk falling or scattering during removal
🛑 STOP WORK if: weather conditions (wind speed exceeds manufacturer limits or visibility poor) prevent safe derrig operations
admin: Record exclusion zone briefing attendance and time before derrig starts
Verify crane operator holds current ticket and has conducted pre-use check
Confirm engineer-approved removal sequence is on site and followed in order
Complete site walkover and photograph cleared condition before handover to next trade

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone is barricaded and no workers or vehicles are within 1.5 times crane radius during movement
monitoring.who: Supervisor / Traffic control personnel / Crane operator
monitoring.frequency: continuous during all crane movement and derrig operations
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation that zone is clear; no personnel within barrier; exclusion zone briefing sheet signed by all workers

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

inference.hrcw_category: WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.8 — Work involving use of explosives or crane
inference.hrcw_license_class: Crane Licence — C6 (mobile crane), C2 (tower crane), or relevant class
ppe: Hard hat where overhead risk present
Full body harness — when working at height attaching or releasing lifting inserts
Hi-vis Class D day/night vest or shirt
certifications: Traffic Control accreditation — TCP and TCS minimum
Roads and Maritime Services road opening permit
First aid — at least one trained first aider on site
Crane operator licence — C6 mobile crane or C2 tower crane (SafeWork NSW)
Rigger licence — RB basic, RI intermediate, or RA advanced (SafeWork NSW)
Rigging gear inspection — pre-use inspection logged before each use
Traffic controller accreditation — current TCS (Traffic Controller) and TCP (Traffic Control Plan) certification
permits: Road opening permit — Transport for NSW or council before any road cut
Traffic Management Plan — approved before work commences
Lane closure approval — Transport for NSW where state road affected
Speed reduction approval — Transport for NSW or council
Lift study — documented before every critical lift
Ground bearing assessment — engineer certification before mobile crane setup
Crane exclusion zone — established and enforced before lift commences
Outrigger mat design — engineer-certified where soft or uncertain ground
Crane set-up permit — ground bearing capacity confirmed before outriggers deployed
Bracing design — engineer-certified bracing layout required before first panel erected
Engineer approval — written approval from structural engineer required before any temporary bracing removed
Written approval from project design engineer or independent qualified engineer — required before removing temporary bracing from precast elements
Lift plan — documented and signed before each lift
qualifications: Accredited traffic controller — on site whenever traffic affected
Reinstatement — temporary reinstatement within 24 hours of completion
Exclusion zone — minimum distance from live traffic lanes enforced
Lift supervisor — responsible person designated for every lift
Wind speed limit — maximum defined in lift study, anemometer on site
Pre-lift inspection — daily pre-use check logged before first lift
Outrigger pads — design verified for ground bearing capacity by competent person before lift
Communication — dogman/rigger on continuous two-way communication with crane operator during lift
Erection sequence — engineer-certified sequence; no deviation without engineer sign-off
Brace footings — must achieve specified concrete strength before bracing is loaded; verified by engineer
Lifting insert testing — pull-out capacity tested to AS 3850 before panel is lifted
Rigging register — all lifting gear tagged and within inspection period
SWL marking — every sling, shackle and hook must show SWL
Discard criteria — rigging gear with cuts, kinks or corrosion must be removed
Traffic management arrangement accepted by principal contractor before any works in road corridor
Temporary speed zone signs installed and confirmed before workers enter live lane area
notifications: Transport for NSW — 5 business days before state road work
Council — road opening permit application minimum 5 business days
Utility authorities — Dial Before You Dig before any road cutting
Emergency services — notification of road closures affecting access
Airspace authority — CASA notification where crane exceeds 110m AGL
SafeWork NSW notification — where road works are notifiable HRCW
regulatory_notes: Roads Act 1993 (NSW) — road opening permit mandatory
AS 1742.3 — Traffic control devices for works on roads
Permanent reinstatement — within 30 days of temporary reinstatement
SafeWork NSW — Traffic Management Code of Practice
Exclusion zone — minimum 1m from live traffic lane edge, barriers preferred
AS 2550 — Cranes, hoists and winches — safe use
Critical lift — any lift over 75% capacity, tandem lift, or near powerlines
Dogman — must maintain visual contact with load at all times
WHS Reg 2017 r.211-240 — plant with potential to cause harm; registration, inspection, and operator licence obligations
Wind limits — all crane operations suspended in sustained winds exceeding manufacturer's rated limit (typically 48-72km/h depending on crane and jib configuration)
Tagline required — unguided loads create uncontrolled swing hazard; taglines used on all loads except where impracticable
Load chart — operator must verify SWL for the specific radius and jib configuration before lift
WHS Reg 2017 Schedule 3 cl.5 — tilt-up and precast is notifiable HRCW
AS 3850 — Tilt-up concrete and precast concrete elements — lifting insert requirements
Shop drawings — must be approved by structural engineer and on site before erection commences
Birth certificates — required for each precast element; records mix design, strength test results, and lifting insert certification
Concrete strength — must reach design MPa (verified by compressive strength test report) before any element is lifted
Temporary bracing — remains in place until engineer certifies permanent structure can take load
Tag lines — required on all panels to control rotation during lift
Wind speed — erection suspended in sustained winds exceeding manufacturer/engineer limits for the specific panel size
Adjacent panel bracing — brace second panel before unhooking crane from first panel
AS 3569 — Steel wire ropes
AS 1353 — Flat webbing slings
AS 4497 — Round slings
SWL — never exceed Safe Working Load, apply derated values for angled slings
WHS Reg 2017 Part 5.2 — General duties for plant
Crane set-up on firm level ground — outrigger pads required
WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.14 — work on or adjacent to a traffic corridor is HRCW
Workers must not enter live lane area until traffic management is in place and accepted
